purpose: Represent repair-state timing across skin, heart and tendon without forcing incomparable absolute days into a false universal clock; retain spinal cord as an independent matrix-resolution control.

frozen_rules.causal_requirement: A tissue-level EXIT claim requires a perturbation that changes persistence or clearance of a defined activated repair-state cell population and changes an objective repair outcome.
frozen_rules.timing_rule: Do not infer that more EXIT is always beneficial; classify whether depletion occurs before, near, or after structural stabilization.
frozen_rules.normalization_rule: A dimensionless cross-tissue clock may be calculated only when activation onset, a stabilization/resolution transition, and a comparable resolution endpoint are empirically anchored in the same repair-state lineage or state.
frozen_rules.half_life_rule: Do not label intervention-associated depletion, sparse terminal endpoints, or single-interval signaling decay as a biological wound-state half-life.

shared_architecture: pathological persistence if EXIT is delayed or incomplete

skin.intervention: FMOD administered at surgery; apoptosis is preferentially observed in activated myofibroblasts

anchors.event: full-thickness wound creation, FMOD/control administration and primary suture closure
rat terminal endpoint: FMOD group shows lower alpha-SMA-positive cell density and higher cleaved-caspase-3-positive cell density with reduced scar burden
red Duroc pig terminal endpoint under excessive mechanical loading: lower alpha-SMA-positive persistence and higher cleaved-caspase-3-positive cell density with reduced scar burden

source_data_summary.note: PLA kinetics describe IL1R1-complex signaling in vitro and are not the in-vivo wound-state clock.

safe_exit_onset.reason: FMOD is present from surgery and published in-vivo activated-cell measurements are sparse terminal endpoints; there is no late-only dosing series or dense post-closure alpha-SMA lineage decay curve.

repair_states.F_Act: CD248-positive late-activated fibroblast population targeted by BBIR-T

anchors.event: F-Myo is present; F-Act is detectable in peri-infarct myocardium
F-Myo peaks; infarct scar described as almost mature; CD248-targeted BBIR-T dosing begins
F-Act surpasses F-Myo as the dominant fibroblast subpopulation

anchors.time: approximately day 23 under the published 3-day dosing cadence
anchors.event: after three BBIR-T injections, CD248-positive cells are reduced by approximately two-thirds
anchors.caveat: This is reconstructed from the stated day-14 start and every-3-day dosing/assessment schedule; it is not a biological half-life.

anchors.event: F-Myo approaches baseline while F-Act remains persistently activated without targeted clearance

safe_exit_onset.meaning: Selective depletion initiated when the scar was almost mature improved fibrosis/remodeling outcomes.
safe_exit_onset.lineage_specificity_warning: Do not transfer this timing to the earlier reparative F-Myo population.

heart.intervention_clearance_timescale: A ~2/3 reduction after three discrete BBIR-T doses is a treatment-response milestone, not an exponential natural decay constant.

repair_states.natural_resolution_readout: alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblasts, nearly all actively Scx-expressing during their transient presence

anchors.event: local diphtheria-toxin-induced apoptosis of Scx-lineage cells
anchors.outcome: D28 structural/function restoration is impaired and the repair program is transiently stalled near the proliferative state

anchors.event: alpha-SMA-positive cells persist but are markedly reduced; remodeling phase
alpha-SMA-positive cells are no longer detected in injured tendons
mechanical properties of the D14-18 depleted repairs are no longer significantly different from WT

natural_resolution_onset.bracket: after the D21 peak and by D28
natural_resolution_onset.note: This is an observational physiological transition, not proof that an artificial depletion beginning in this interval would be beneficial.

papers.finding: monocyte-derived macrophage depletion/reconstitution and MMP-13 competence causally control CSPG scar-matrix resolution and functional recovery
key_times: day 7 approximately half of infiltrating monocytes CD11c-positive

papers.finding: reducing generation of pericyte-derived scar-forming progeny reduces fibrosis/ECM and promotes recovery, but this perturbs scar generation rather than post-use cell EXIT

matrix_resolution_control.interpretation: The control supports the general importance of timed resolution while remaining outside the strict activated-cell EXIT count.

why_not_yet: skin lacks a dense in-vivo activated-cell decay trajectory or late-only intervention series
heart has a strong target-specific day-14 safe intervention anchor but no natural F-Act resolution endpoint in the observed day-7 to day-28 window
tendon has the best natural trajectory, but the causal depletion target is broader than the alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblast readout

provisional_clock_logic.adaptive_zone: activated repair cells are still required for closure, matrix deposition, organization or structural stabilization
provisional_clock_logic.transition_zone: repair-state population reaches peak/plateau while tissue enters remodeling and selective late states become dispensable or maladaptive
provisional_clock_logic.resolution_zone: natural or selective EXIT can proceed without loss of structural integrity
provisional_clock_logic.persistence_hazard_zone: activated state remains after its useful structural role and contributes to continuing fibrosis/scar expansion

next_killer_measurements.measurement: same-lineage in-vivo alpha-SMA or lineage-traced myofibroblast density at multiple points spanning closure through D14, in control and FMOD; ideally add delayed FMOD-start arms
next_killer_measurements.goal: identify natural and FMOD-shifted decay curves and the earliest non-harmful EXIT window

next_killer_measurements.measurement: point-level CD248-positive F-Act abundance immediately before each BBIR-T dose and at dense intervals after the third dose, plus later untreated natural-history points beyond D28
next_killer_measurements.goal: separate treatment clearance kinetics from natural persistence and estimate a state-specific clearance constant

next_killer_measurements.measurement: extract point-level alpha-SMA density across D7, D14, D21, D28, D35 and D42 and test a later, narrower Scx/myofibroblast-selective depletion window after the D21 peak
next_killer_measurements.goal: convert the observed natural-resolution bracket into a causal safe-exit boundary

gate_decision.strongest_conclusion: Across skin, heart and tendon, repair outcome depends not merely on whether activated repair-state cells exit, but on cell identity and timing relative to tissue stabilization. Current evidence supports a cross-tissue timing gate but does not yet identify a universal numerical resolution window.
gate_decision.next_version_gate: EXIT_CLOCK_v0.2 requires at least two tissues with dense same-state decay trajectories plus a causally bounded safe-exit onset.
